answer: When a backbone link flaps, routing updates ripple out with timing that depends on a network's position, so a claimant logs the arrival times of the next flap and its update sequence must match its neighbours' sequences. A ferrous cored router in a faraway datacentre sees a different order and delay, so copied logs fail the sequence check; no haven of identical reports survives, since flaps are unpredictable and public, and the river of updates flows past each network at its own speed.
